title: Conservation strategies
group: BIO-EVOL / BIO-ECOL / BIO-PLANT — Evolution, Ecology & Plants
examples: What is the difference between in-situ and ex-situ conservation?
Can you give an example of a protected area?
Which method is better for saving a whole ecosystem?

explain.say: Today we will learn about ways to save plants and animals.
First we look at in-situ conservation methods.
In-situ means conserving species in their natural place.
Next we study ex-situ conservation methods.
Ex-situ means keeping species safe outside their natural home.
Protected areas are specific places set aside for conservation.

faq.q: What is the main difference between in-situ and ex-situ?
faq.a: In-situ means protecting a species where it naturally lives. Ex-situ means taking it somewhere else for safety.
asks: Can you compare the two methods?
Is it better to keep them in the wild or in a garden?

faq.q: Are all protected areas the same?
faq.a: No, protected areas have different levels of protection. Some allow limited human activity.
asks: What is the difference between a park and a reserve?
Do all protected areas stop all human activity?

faq.q: Why do we need both kinds of conservation?
faq.a: We use both because they protect different things. In-situ keeps the system whole, and ex-situ acts as a backup.
asks: Why not just use protected areas?
What if the wild area changes too much?

faq.a: A seed bank is a place where seeds from many different plants are stored safely. This keeps the genetic information alive.

faq.q: What does 'biodiversity' mean in this context?
faq.a: Biodiversity means the variety of life in a place. Conservation aims to keep this variety high.

facts: In-situ conservation protects species within their natural habitat.
Ex-situ conservation involves keeping species outside their natural habitat.
Protected areas are legally designated zones for conservation.
Seed banks store genetic material from plant species.

quiz.say: Saving a rare monkey in its actual forest habitat is an example of:
quiz.why: In-situ means keeping the species in its original, natural environment.

wrong.0: This is too general; it names a location type, not the method.
wrong.1: This is wrong because seed banking is a specific ex-situ technique.
wrong.3: This is wrong because ex-situ means moving it outside the natural habitat.

quiz.say: Storing seeds from many different grasses in a cool facility is:
quiz.why: Storing seeds away from their natural growing place is the definition of ex-situ conservation.

wrong.0: A National Park is a type of protected area, not the storage method itself.
wrong.1: In-situ requires the seeds to be in the actual growing environment.
wrong.2: Biodiversity is what we are trying to save, not the method of saving.

quiz.say: A designated area with strict rules to protect a specific group of animals is called a:
quiz.why: Protected areas are official zones established by law for conservation purposes.

wrong.0: A zoo is a facility, which is a type of ex-situ conservation, not the general area type.
wrong.1: A seed bank is a storage facility, not a geographical protected zone.
wrong.2: An ecosystem is the community itself, while a protected area is the legal boundary around it.
